note: Every Minecraft artifact this repository downloads, pinned by content hash. Nothing is vendored: the jars are fetched into .tmp/ and verified before use, so a clone stays small and a tampered mirror is caught rather than compiled against. The server build and the API build are the SAME build (26.3 build 231), so the plugin is compiled against exactly the server it is tested on.

java.why: Paper 26.3 refuses to start on anything older. macOS ships a /usr/bin/java stub that is not a JVM at all, so this path is used explicitly rather than trusting PATH.

world.why: The human-playable server (npm run mc:server, npm run mc:up -- --keep) generates ORDINARY TERRAIN. It used to be minecraft:flat with default generator settings, which is bedrock, two dirt and one grass: no ores, no trees, no caves. The economy trades iron_ingot, oak_log, stone, glass, coal, copper_ingot, oak_planks and redstone, so not one of the eight materials existed in the world a player spawned into, and GAME_LOOP.md's first core action -- "Mine, chop, or harvest one stack-worth of a material" -- was impossible. The seed is pinned so the world is the same one every time and /nearcraft world-selftest means something. The BOT fixture in scripts/mc-bot.mjs deliberately keeps a flat world: it never sends position packets, so real terrain could leave it in water or inside a block, and the bot proves settlement rather than scenery.

adventure-key.use: compile only — Paper's own supertypes reference it, so javac needs it even though this plugin does not

adventure-api.use: compile only — CommandSender is an Audience

annotations.use: compile only — Paper annotates its API with @NotNull, and javac must resolve the annotation type

guava.use: compile only — Bukkit returns a Multimap from Material.getItemAttributes

bungeecord-chat.use: compile only — sendMessage is overloaded on BaseComponent, so javac must see the type to pick the String overload

paper.use: the server npm run mc:server boots

ViaVersion.use: server plugin, bot runs only - lets a 1.21.11 protocol client reach a 26.3 server

ViaBackwards.use: server plugin, bot runs only - lets a 1.21.11 protocol client reach a 26.3 server

bot.why: A headless client has no Mojang account, so the bot server runs online-mode=false. That applies to npm run mc:bot ONLY, in its own directory; npm run mc:server keeps online-mode=true. mineflayer speaks 1.21.11 and ViaVersion bridges it to this 26.3 server - the combination the sibling EthCraft repository records as working against this exact Paper build. Paper rejects this client position packets with "Invalid move player packet received" (a hard NaN/range check on the packet values, not a moved-wrongly threshold), because the translation mangles the field layout. Trying 26.1, the newest protocol mineflayer supports, got LESS far. So the harness simply does not send position packets: a client that never moves does not need them.
